Re: Joe Derrane’s

Paddy O’Brien (Offaly) thinks that Hardiman’s Fancy and Hardiman the Fiddler are named
after the same man.

Google AI generated blurb disagrees stating:
“Hardiman the Fiddler” refers to a popular Irish traditional slip jig, named after James Hardiman (1782–1855),
an important Irish historian, librarian (at Queen’s College, Galway), and music collector known for
his work on Irish history and culture.

From an article by Nick Whitmer we have:
Martin Hardiman was elected secretary of the Irish Music Club of Chicago in July 1908.
Hardiman was a dancer and dance teacher, and associated with the well-known Chicago
dancing teacher John E. McNamara, also a club member.

A Google search also says the Hardiman the Fiddler first appeared in print in O’Neill’s
Music of Ireland, 1903. So, I would tend to think that Paddy is correct in his belief that
both tunes are named for Martin Hardiman.

↳ Posted by ithaca-markb on December 30th, 2025.
